## Q6
If in Delhi, the number of employees who work in Accounts is 40% more than the number who work in HR, what is the number of employees who work in IT in Delhi?

The following table shows the number of employees in an organization in five cities. The total number of employees is 4,260. Percentages show distribution across HR, Finance, IT and Accounts. Some values are missing and may be calculated when required. Each employee works in only one department.

| City | Employees | HR | Finance | IT | Accounts |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Delhi | 900 | - | 18% | - | 28% |
| Mumbai | 760 | 15% | - | 30% | - |
| Bengaluru | - | 18% | 20% | - | 32% |
| Hyderabad | - | - | 25% | 18% | 35% |
| Gurgaon | 700 | 20% | 22% | - | 20% |

## Q6 - Options
(A) 266
(B) 306
(C) 352
(D) 294

## Q6 - Hint
**Answer:** B
**Topic:** Data Interpretation
**Source:** UGC NET Jun 2023 (17 Jun, Shift 1) · Paper 1 · Q1

In Delhi, total employees = 900. Accounts = 28% of 900 = 252.<br>
The number of Accounts employees is 40% more than HR employees. Let HR employees be x.<br>
x + 0.4x = 252 -&gt; 1.4x = 252 -&gt; x = 180.<br>
HR percentage = (180 / 900) \* 100 = 20%.<br>
Total percentage of HR, Finance, and Accounts = 20% + 18% + 28% = 66%.<br>
Therefore, IT percentage = 100% - 66% = 34%.<br>
Number of IT employees in Delhi = 34% of 900 = 306.

**Answer:** B
**Topic:** Data Interpretation
**Source:** UGC NET Jun 2023 (17 Jun, Shift 1) · Paper 1 · Q3

The total number of employees across all five cities is 4260.<br>
Employees in Delhi + Mumbai + Gurgaon = 900 + 760 + 700 = 2360.<br>
Employees in Bengaluru + Hyderabad = 4260 - 2360 = 1900.<br>
Let the number of employees in Hyderabad be H. The number in Bengaluru is 0.9H.<br>
0.9H + H = 1900 -&gt; 1.9H = 1900 -&gt; H = 1000. So, Bengaluru has 900 employees.<br>

Total Finance = 180 + 250 = 430.<br>
Total Accounts = 288 + 350 = 638.<br>
Difference = 638 - 430 = 208.

## Q16 - Hint
**Answer:** A
**Topic:** Data Interpretation
**Source:** UGC NET Mar 2023 (11 Mar, Shift 2) · Paper 1 · Q1

For each friend, Monthly Income = Salary + Incentive = 1.15 × Salary (since Incentive = 15% of Salary). Total expenditure is 60% of monthly income (since 40% is saved):

- (b) Incentive amounts to 15% of salary.
- (c) All six friends save 40% of their monthly income.
- (d) There is no expenditure other than those given in the table.

## Q19 - Options
(A) 4,600
(B) 52,200
(C) 55,200
(D) 4,900

## Q19 - Hint
**Answer:** C
**Topic:** Data Interpretation
**Source:** UGC NET Mar 2023 (11 Mar, Shift 2) · Paper 1 · Q4

Monthly income of A = ₹92,000 + 15% of ₹92,000 = ₹92,000 + ₹13,800 = ₹1,05,800.<br>
Monthly income of D = ₹88,000 + 15% of ₹88,000 = ₹88,000 + ₹13,200 = ₹1,01,200.<br>
Difference in monthly income = ₹1,05,800 − ₹1,01,200 = ₹4,600.<br>
The question asks for the annual income difference:<br>
Annual difference = ₹4,600 × 12 = ₹55,200. (Option A of ₹4,600 represents the monthly difference).

## Q20
Expenditure by A on Travelling constitutes approximately \_\_\_\_\_\_ % of the salary of F.

The following table shows the monthly income and various expenditures of six friends A–F in absolute value or in percentage (in terms of monthly income) form. Some values (marked as "–") are missing in the table which you are expected to calculate if required. Based on the data in the table, answer the questions.

**Income and Expenditure Details**

| Friend | Salary (₹) | Incentive (₹) | Travel | Food | Accommodation | Shopping |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| A | 92,000 | – | – | 10,960 | 10% | 15% |
| B | – | 14,400 | 15,280 | 17,000 | 12,400 | – |
| C | – | 12,600 | 12% | 8% | – | 12% |
| D | 88,000 | – | – | 15,120 | 9% | 16,800 |
| E | 80,000 | – | 5% | – | 8,400 | 11,240 |
| F | – | 11,400 | 8,400 | 8% | – | 13,720 |

**Notes:**

- (a) Monthly Income = Salary + Incentive.
- (b) Incentive amounts to 15% of salary.
- (c) All six friends save 40% of their monthly income.
- (d) There is no expenditure other than those given in the table.

## Q20 - Options
(A) 30
(B) 38
(C) 32
(D) 34

## Q20 - Hint
**Answer:** D
**Topic:** Data Interpretation
**Source:** UGC NET Mar 2023 (11 Mar, Shift 2) · Paper 1 · Q5

Friend A has a monthly income of ₹1,05,800 and total expenditure (60%) of ₹63,480. Given Food = ₹10,960, Accommodation (10%) = ₹10,580, and Shopping (15%) = ₹15,870, Travelling expenditure for A = 63,480 − (10,960 + 10,580 + 15,870) = ₹26,070.<br>
For Friend F, incentive of ₹11,400 represents 15% of salary, so Salary of F = 11,400 / 0.15 = ₹76,000.<br>
Percentage = (26,070 / 76,000) × 100 ≈ 34.30%, which is approximately 34%.
